land.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

predecessors.note: The Heruli page: after Nedao (454) they 'were subsequently among the several peoples now able to consolidate a kingdom near the Middle Danube'; the Nedao page has them 'achieving independence' by the early 460s. The huns dossier does not name the Heruli among its successors (Gepids, Ostrogoths, Rugiland, Eastern Roman Empire); a gap-filler should add this one.

land.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

successors.note: The Balkan federates of 512-567 lived on Eastern Roman soil; from 539 only the Roman side of Singidunum is drawn (the Bassianae district passes to the Gepid dossier's land). The Heruli page says only that the polity 'disappears from the surviving historical records' after one generation in the Belgrade area, 'apparently replaced by the incoming Avars'. The Danubian kingdom of 460-494 ends in 494 with no named heir (ledger 494): the Heruli and Lombards pages are silent on who held the land.

correction.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 460-494: the Danubian kingdom, redrawn 2026-10-24 after review. The page has no map, infobox or area: 'Procopius describes it as being north of the Danube', sharing a border with the Rugians 'stretching along the Danube in what is now Lower Austria'; 'many scholars assume they lived to the east of the Rugii, in southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia'; Prostko-Prostynski puts it further west (Rugiland in northeastern Lower Austria, or southwestern Bohemia), which is not drawn because the Lombards occupy the Rugian country in 488 (Heruli and Lombards pages). Shape: admin1 Jihomoravsky (Czechia) plus Bratislavsky and Trnavsky kraj (Slovakia), 55 cells, about 13,900 km2 (gazetteer, 2026-10-24). The first draft used a 40 km disc round Bratislava; it crossed the Danube (7 of its 49 cells in ostrogoths_455, 3 in danubian-suebi_453), against Procopius's 'north of the Danube'. The new shape has no cell in ostrogoths_454/455, danubian-suebi (now Nitriansky kraj, which adjoins Trnavsky kraj without sharing a cell), sciri_454 or kingdom-of-odoacer; it shares only border cells with rugiland_455/476/480 (1 cell), lombards_480 (2), lombards_488/490 (1 each). Army estimate 5,000-10,000 men (Heather) suggests a small realm. After Bolia (c. 469) 'some scholars' think land south of the Danube in Pannonia was gained; Prostko-Prostynski keeps it 'restricted to the area north of the Danube': the north-bank shape is kept. 494 is Procopius's end; the page notes estimates of 493-511 (the Lombards page repeats them). Infobox area: none on the page.

correction.text: Bassianae, where the Heruli were first moved in 512: 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 512-526: the first federate settlement, Bassianae. Heruli page: 'a large part of the Heruli crossed the Danube into Roman territory' (Marcellinus Comes dates this to 512) and were 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'. The Bassianae page (read 2026-10-24) gives no coordinates, so the area is drawn as admin1 Sremski (Syrmia, Serbia) inside a 70 km disc round Belgrade: 9 cells, about 2,300 km2, a placeholder for the district. Why the land counts as Roman: the Bassianae page says 'In 510 AD, the treaty between Eastern Roman Empire and Ostrogoths divided the Syrmia region between two countries' and that Bassianae went to the Eastern Roman state. The neighbour dossiers differ and this is flagged: ostrogothic-kingdom_510 (which holds the Sirmium district 504-536) has 5 of the 9 cells, kingdom-of-the-gepids_510 has 1, 3 cells lie in no neighbour shape and eastern-roman-empire_510 has none; the owners of ostrogothic-kingdom and eastern-roman-empire should reconcile Syrmia east of Sirmium for 510-536 with the Bassianae page. The first draft drew a 70 km disc round Belgrade (57 cells, about 14,400 km2) for 512-567, of which only 7 cells were Eastern Roman (16 Gepid and 10 Ostrogothic in 510).

correction.text: Bassianae (Syrmia) and the Roman side of Singidunum (Moesia), 527-538

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 527-538: Bassianae plus the Singidunum grant. Heruli page: 'the remaining Heruli were given land near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia by Emperor Justinian' 'after he became emperor in 527'; the page gives no year for the grant, so 527 is the lower bound (the Grepes page the reviewer named does not exist on Wikipedia, url_not_found 2026-10-24). The Roman side of Singidunum is drawn as the 70 km Belgrade disc intersected with eastern-roman-empire_523: 7 cells, about 1,800 km2, all inside eastern-roman-empire_510 to _567, so it overlaps no other dossier in any year. The page says 'first ... later', which may mean the Heruli left Bassianae; the shape keeps both districts because the page does not say Bassianae was given up. The Bassianae part keeps the overlaps flagged in heruli_512 until 538.

correction.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 539-567: the Roman side of Singidunum only. From 539 the Bassianae district (Syrmia) is held by kingdom-of-the-gepids (gepids_539 has all 9 cells, gepids_536 has 6; its ledger has the Gepids take Sirmium in 536 and the Singidunum bank in 539), and the Heruli page has the revolt of about 545-548 end with 'two thirds of the Heruli' submitting 'themselves to the Gepids'. The Heruli page dates no transfer of Bassianae, so the 539 loss is a confidence-1 bridge to the neighbour's shape. What stays is the 7-cell Roman side (no overlap with any Gepid, Ostrogothic or Lombard shape). Gepid shapes also hold 15 of the 27 cells south of the Sava and Danube inside the 70 km disc (gepids_539), which is why the first draft's disc was mostly Gepid land from 539. The page's last words are 'After one generation in the Belgrade area, the Herulian federate polity in the Balkans disappears from the surviving historical records, apparently replaced by the incoming Avars'; 567 (Sinduald's execution in Italy) is the last date on the page, so the end year is a bridge.

region.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

ledger.note: 460: the Heruli consolidate a kingdom on the Middle Danube. Nedao page: 'by the early 460s the Hunnic Empire dissolved, with the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Suebi, and Ostrogoths achieving independence'; Heruli page: 'They were subsequently among the several peoples now able to consolidate a kingdom near the Middle Danube' and 'Procopius describes it as being north of the Danube'. Neither page gives a founding year or a capital; 460 is the early-460s reading. The site of the kingdom is disputed (southern Moravia or south-western Slovakia, or north-eastern Lower Austria, which the rugiland dossier gives to the Rugii until 487).

region.text: the Langobardi, then settled in the Rugian country after 488, made to pay tribute to the Heruli by 491

ledger.note: 491: the Heruli make the Lombards pay tribute. 'by the time Anastasius became emperor in 491 the Heruli had forced the Langobardi' to pay tribute. The page dates the subjugation only by this terminus; the Lombards had occupied the abandoned Rugian country in 488 (Heruli page) and Odoacer's page has it 'settled by the Lombards by 493'.

region.text: the Langobardi, then settled in the Rugian country after 488, made to pay tribute to the Heruli by 491

ledger.note: 494: Rodulf attacks the Lombards and the tribute ends. 'only three years later, in 494, King Rodulf was pressured by his followers to attack the Lombards' (Procopius); Rodulf died in the battle. Paul the Deacon places Rodulf's defeat at 'approximately 494-511' and the page gives estimates of 493-511 for the fall of the kingdom.

region.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

ledger.note: 494: the Danubian kingdom falls. Rodulf died in the battle and, in the page's words, 'the Heruli kingdom came to an end' (Procopius's date); 'The Heruli had to move from the territory they had been holding' and 'moved around in the regions beyond the Danube'. Neither the Heruli page nor the Lombards page (both read 2026-10-24) says who held the land afterwards: the Lombards page puts the Lombards on the 'Feld' (the Little Alfold) and in the Rugian country, and says nothing of Moravia or south-western Slovakia. The counterpart is therefore 'nobody' (confidence 1, a bridge); the lombards dossier (eu-06-e) holds only 2 of the 49 cells of the first draft, so no gain is expected there. The Heruli of Italy under Odoacer ('The Heruli in Italy suffered badly when Odoacer was defeated' in 493) are not this kingdom.

region.text: Bassianae, where the Heruli were first moved in 512: 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'

ledger.note: 512: the Heruli cross the Danube into the Roman Empire. 'Marcellinus Comes dates this to 512'; they were 'welcomed by Emperor Anastasius I' and the main group was first moved to the area of Bassianae; one group 'went north and settled in Thule' (Scandinavia). The region is the Bassianae district only; the Singidunum grant is the 527 gain. The land counts as Roman by the Bassianae page (Syrmia divided by the 510 treaty, Bassianae to the Eastern Roman state), but ostrogothic-kingdom_510 holds 5 of its 9 cells (see heruli_512).

region.text: Bassianae, where the Heruli were first moved in 512: 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'

ledger.note: 512: the Heruli become Roman federates in the Balkans. The page's closing sentence calls them 'the Herulian federate polity in the Balkans'; the dossier follows the burgundian-kingdom model, in which Roman federates are drawn in the lighter tint with the empire as counterpart.

region.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

ledger.note: After 527: Justinian gives land near Singidunum. 'the remaining Heruli were given land near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia by Emperor Justinian' 'after he became emperor in 527'; the king Grepes converted to Orthodoxy in 528. The page gives no year for the grant, so 527 is the page's lower bound (confidence 1); the Grepes and Sinduald pages do not exist on Wikipedia (url_not_found). The region is the Roman side of Singidunum (south of the Sava and the Danube), not the Bassianae district of 512.

region.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

ledger.note: After 527: the Singidunum land is held as a Roman federate colony (the page's 'Herulian federate polity in the Balkans'); the year is the grant's lower bound, as in the 527 gain.

region.text: Bassianae, where the Heruli were first moved in 512: 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'

ledger.note: 539: the Bassianae district leaves the Roman federation: the Gepid dossier holds all of it from 539 (6 of 9 cells from 536). The Heruli page dates only the revolt of about 545-548, after which 'two thirds of the Heruli' submitted 'themselves to the Gepids'; the year is a bridge to the neighbour's shape.

region.text: Bassianae, where the Heruli were first moved in 512: 'moved first to the area of Bassianae (near modern Donji Petrovci) in an eastern part of Pannonia north of Belgrade'

ledger.note: 539: the Bassianae district passes to the Gepids. The Heruli page says 'Fearing the reaction of the Romans, the supporters of Datius, two thirds of the Heruli, submitted themselves to the Gepids' during the revolt of about 545-548; it does not date a transfer of land, so 539 is the year the Gepid dossier's shape takes the district (confidence 1). The Gepid ledger records its 536 and 539 gains as coming from the Eastern Roman Empire, not from the Heruli: a gap-filler may wish to name heruli there.

region.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

ledger.note: 567: the last dated Herulian item. Sinduald 'was declared king of the Heruli' in 566 and 'was executed by Narses in 567' (he ruled the Breoni in Italy; 'the last historically attested Herule'); 'After one generation in the Belgrade area, the Herulian federate polity in the Balkans disappears from the surviving historical records, apparently replaced by the incoming Avars'. The page does not date the end of the Balkan federation (the Sinduald page does not exist on Wikipedia), so 567 is a bridge (confidence 1); the mid-540s revolt and the 552 shipment of 3,000 horsemen to Italy shrank it.

region.text: the land 'near Singidunum (modern Belgrade) in Moesia' given by Justinian 'after he became emperor in 527': the Roman side, south of the Sava and the Danube

ledger.note: 567: the Heruli polity ends. 'the Herulian federate polity in the Balkans disappears from the surviving historical records' (apparently replaced by the Avars, the page adds); 567 is the year of Sinduald's execution, the last date on the page. The Avars page (avar-khaganate dossier) has the Avars at the Sava and in Pannonia from 568.

wars.name: Battle of Bolia
wars.outcome: Ostrogothic victory 'achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; the Heruli are listed in the opposing coalition. No Herulian land is named as lost.
wars.note: The Odoacer page dates it 468 and 'about 469'. The Heruli page: 'some scholars' think the Heruli gained land south of the Danube in Pannonia after Bolia; disputed, not drawn.

wars.name: Herulian-Lombard war

zones.text: the kingdom 'north of the Danube' bordering the Rugians on the Danube: 'southern Moravia or southwestern Slovakia' (many scholars)

wars.outcome: Rodulf attacks the Lombards in 494 and is killed; the Heruli kingdom ends (Procopius); Paul the Deacon puts it between 494 and 511.
wars.note: Zone: the Herulian kingdom, the land that changes hands in the ledger (494 loss). The page does not name the battlefield.

wars.name: Theoderic's campaign against the Heruli
wars.outcome: Ennodius's panegyric indicates Theoderic's forces killed 'large numbers of Heruli' at their own settlements after an attack on Theoderic.
wars.note: 507 is Ennodius's date as the page gives it; the page does not locate the settlements, so no zone.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for either phase; the Danubian kingdom is placed by the disputed readings of Procopius (three admin1 units north of the Danube), the Balkan colony by two place names (Bassianae, Singidunum) drawn as a district and a disc part; 495-511 is a gap in which no polity is drawn.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-d and eu-06-e (counterparts_needing_dossiers) and named in the eu-06 scope (Rugii, Heruli, Sciri and Suebi of the Danube). Four pages opened; the Rodulf page is a disambiguation and was not used. One dossier for two phases: the Danubian kingdom (460-494) and the Balkan federates (512-567), with 495-511 empty. The Heruli of Odoacer's army (476-493), of Narses's army (552) and of Sinduald's Breoni (554-567) were soldiers and settlers in Italy, not territory, and are not drawn here. Capitals: the page names none; the list is empty. Rulers: Rodulf (d. 494), Grepes (528), Ochus, Datius and Sinduald (566-567) are named, but not as a documented list with reign years. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: no region name for south-western Slovakia, so a 40 km disc round Bratislava is used. Cliopatria rows nearby: Rugiland 455-489, Lombards 480-586, Ostrogoths 455-499; the Lombards dossier has no 491-494 events for the Herulian tribute or the 494 gain, and the huns dossier does not list the Heruli as a successor. Repair of 2026-10-24 (review eu-06-x): the 40 km Bratislava disc and the 70 km Belgrade disc were replaced. Kingdom: Jihomoravsky plus Bratislavsky and Trnavsky kraj (all north of the Danube). Balkan phase: heruli_512 (Bassianae, Sremski inside the Belgrade disc), heruli_527 (plus the Roman side of Singidunum, the disc intersected with eastern-roman-empire_523), heruli_539 (Singidunum side only, the Bassianae district going to the Gepids). The 512 and 527 gains no longer share a region. The 494 loss now has counterpart 'nobody' (pages silent). Pages tried and not found: Grepes, Sinduald, Sindual (url_not_found). Gazetteer names wanted: Bassianae (place, Donji Petrovci, Ruma, Syrmia), Singidunum (alias of Belgrade already). Overlaps left: the Bassianae district 512-538 shares 5 of 9 cells with ostrogothic-kingdom_510/534 and 1 with kingdom-of-the-gepids_510; border cells with rugiland and lombards in 460-494.
